who: Antony Gerald (A. G.) Hopkins, historian of Africa and imperialism at the University of Texas at Austin; PhD London 1964.

evidence.says: His August 2012 CV names Antony Gerald Hopkins, lists the Texas history chair from 2002, and records a London PhD in 1964 on the economic history of Lagos.
The Antony Hopkins authority identifies a composer, pianist and music broadcaster, with works including Lady Rohesia.
The A. Grosvenor Hopkins authority expands the name to Abel Grosvenor Hopkins and cites The Agricola and Germania (1893).

notes: None of the supplied candidates is Antony Gerald Hopkins. The exact-name heading is a musician; the other headings expand to different names or concern unrelated works.

who: Dean Rehberger, Michigan State University historian and digital humanities scholar; PhD University of Utah.

evidence.says: The August 2025 departmental announcement identifies Dean Rehberger as an associate professor of history and the outgoing Matrix director after eighteen years.
The university faculty catalogue lists Dean A. Rehberger with a PhD from the University of Utah.
The authority identifies Dean Rehberger with Michigan State University through the Enslaved project advisory board.

notes: The authority affiliation, university appointment and Utah doctorate agree with the supervisor record.

who: Jerma A. Jackson, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill historian of gospel music; PhD Rutgers.

who: Christopher Kent, University of Saskatchewan historian of Victorian Britain; DPhil Sussex 1969.

The authority identifies Christopher Kent as the author of Brains and Numbers (1978).

notes: The matching book, doctorate, institution and direct advisor credit establish the identity. The repository dates the supplied student title to a 2005 MA, differing from the AHA record's 2015 dissertation metadata.
